claim: Cd300a−/− mice showed larger tumor volume than wild-type mice after transplantation of B16 melanoma.
source: The Cd300a−/− mice showed larger tumor volume and shorter survival than did wild-type mice (Figure 1A and B), indicating that CD300a suppresses the development of melanoma.
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing tumor growth curves in Figure 1A comparing wild-type and Cd300a−/− mice.

claim: Cd300a−/− mice showed shorter survival than wild-type mice after transplantation of B16 melanoma.
source: The Cd300a−/− mice showed larger tumor volume and shorter survival than did wild-type mice (Figure 1A and B), indicating that CD300a suppresses the development of melanoma.
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing survival curves in Figure 1B comparing wild-type and Cd300a−/− mice.

claim: CD300a suppresses the development of melanoma.
source: The Cd300a−/− mice showed larger tumor volume and shorter survival than did wild-type mice (Figure 1A and B), indicating that CD300a suppresses the development of melanoma.
evidence: Inference drawn from experimental data showing increased tumor growth and decreased survival in CD300a-deficient mice.

claim: Rag1−/− and Rag1−/−;Cd300a−/− mice showed comparable levels of tumor development after injection of B16 melanoma cells.
source: In contrast, Rag-deficient (Rag1−/−) and Rag1−/−;Cd300a−/− mice showed comparable levels of tumor development and survival after injection of B16 melanoma cells (Figure 1C and D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data in Figure 1C showing tumor growth curves.

claim: The suppressive effect of CD300a on melanoma development is dependent on the adaptive immune response.
source: These results indicate that the suppressive effect of CD300a on melanoma development is dependent on the adaptive immune response.
evidence: Inference based on comparable tumor development in Rag1−/− and Rag1−/−;Cd300a−/− mice, which lack adaptive immunity.

claim: CD300a was not expressed on tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes.
source: However, we also observed that CD300a was not expressed on tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes but was broadly expressed on myeloid cells, including populations of Ly6G+ neutrophils, CD11c+~high DCs, and CD11clowCD11b+ macrophages (Figure 1E).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 1E showing CD300a expression patterns.

claim: CD300a was broadly expressed on myeloid cells, including populations of Ly6G+ neutrophils, CD11c+high DCs, and CD11clowCD11b+ macrophages.
source: However, we also observed that CD300a was not expressed on tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes but was broadly expressed on myeloid cells, including populations of Ly6G+ neutrophils, CD11c+~high DCs, and CD11clowCD11b+ macrophages (Figure 1E).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 1E showing CD300a expression on different myeloid cell populations.

claim: CD300a expressed on myeloid cells suppresses melanoma development via adaptive immune responses.
source: These results suggest that CD300a expressed on myeloid cells suppresses melanoma development via adaptive immune responses.
evidence: Inference based on CD300a expression pattern on myeloid cells and dependence on adaptive immunity.

claim: Cd300afl/fl;ItgaxCre mice expressed CD300a on Ly6G+ cells and CD11c− cells, but not on CD11c+high cells.
source: Cd300afl/fl;ItgaxCre mice expressed CD300a on Ly6G+ cells and CD11c− cells, but not on CD11c+~high cells (Figure 1E).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 1E showing CD300a expression patterns in conditional knockout mice.

claim: Cd300afl/fl;Lyz2Cre mice express CD300a on CD11c+high cells and the subpopulation of CD11clow cells, but not on Ly6G+ cells.
source: In contrast, Cd300afl/fl;Lyz2Cre mice express CD300a on CD11c+~high cells and the subpopulation of CD11clow cells, but not on Ly6G+ cells (Figure 1E).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 1E showing CD300a expression patterns in conditional knockout mice.

claim: Tumor growth was comparable between Cd300afl/fl;Lyz2Cre and Cd300afl/fl mice.
source: Although tumor growth was comparable between Cd300afl/fl;Lyz2Cre and Cd300afl/fl mice, Cd300afl/fl;ItgaxCre mice showed greater tumor volume than did Cd300afl/fl mice (Figure 1F).
evidence: Supported by experimental data in Figure 1F showing tumor growth curves.

claim: Cd300afl/fl;ItgaxCre mice showed greater tumor volume than Cd300afl/fl mice.
source: Although tumor growth was comparable between Cd300afl/fl;Lyz2Cre and Cd300afl/fl mice, Cd300afl/fl;ItgaxCre mice showed greater tumor volume than did Cd300afl/fl mice (Figure 1F).
evidence: Supported by experimental data in Figure 1F showing tumor growth curves.

claim: CD300a on DCs, rather than on neutrophils or macrophages, induces the adaptive immune response to inhibit tumor development.
source: These data implicated CD300a on DCs, rather than on neutrophils or macrophages, in inducing the adaptive immune response to inhibit tumor development.
evidence: Inference based on differential tumor growth in cell-type-specific CD300a knockout mice.

claim: The number of Treg cells in melanoma is correlated with accelerated tumor growth.
source: Previous reports have demonstrated that the number of Treg cells in melanoma is correlated with accelerated tumor growth (Mougiakakos et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature.

claim: Depletion of Treg cells leads to less melanoma growth.
source: In contrast, depletion of Treg cells leads to less melanoma growth.
evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge about Treg cell function in tumors.

claim: The Treg cell population was larger in the tumor of Cd300a−/− mice compared with that of wild-type mice.
source: The Treg cell population was larger in the tumor, but not the draining lymph nodes, of Cd300a−/− mice compared with that of wild-type mice (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry and immunohistochemistry data in Figure 2A and B.

claim: The Treg cell population in draining lymph nodes was comparable between Cd300a−/− mice and wild-type mice.
source: The Treg cell population was larger in the tumor, but not the draining lymph nodes, of Cd300a−/− mice compared with that of wild-type mice (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 2A.

claim: Cd300afl/fl;ItgaxCre mice showed a higher number of tumor-infiltrating Treg cells than Cd300afl/fl mice.
source: Likewise, Cd300afl/fl;ItgaxCre mice showed a higher number of tumor-infiltrating Treg cells than did Cd300afl/fl mice (Figure 2C).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 2C.

claim: Treg cells in Cd300afl/fl;ItgaxCre mice showed higher expression of Ki67 than Cd300afl/fl mice.
source: These Treg cells in Cd300afl/fl;ItgaxCre mice showed higher expression of Ki67 and CTLA-4 than did Cd300afl/fl mice, although the expressions of CD25, GITR, and BCL2 on tumor-infiltrating Treg cells were comparable between two genotypes of mice (Figure 2D and E, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 2D.

claim: Treg cells in Cd300afl/fl;ItgaxCre mice showed higher expression of CTLA-4 than Cd300afl/fl mice.
source: These Treg cells in Cd300afl/fl;ItgaxCre mice showed higher expression of Ki67 and CTLA-4 than did Cd300afl/fl mice, although the expressions of CD25, GITR, and BCL2 on tumor-infiltrating Treg cells were comparable between two genotypes of mice (Figure 2D and E, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 2E.

claim: The expressions of CD25, GITR, and BCL2 on tumor-infiltrating Treg cells were comparable between Cd300afl/fl;ItgaxCre and Cd300afl/fl mice.
source: These Treg cells in Cd300afl/fl;ItgaxCre mice showed higher expression of Ki67 and CTLA-4 than did Cd300afl/fl mice, although the expressions of CD25, GITR, and BCL2 on tumor-infiltrating Treg cells were comparable between two genotypes of mice (Figure 2D and E, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: After Treg cell depletion, the tumor volume of Cd300a−/− mice decreased to a level comparable to that seen in wild-type mice.
source: After Treg cell depletion, the tumor volume of the Cd300a−/− and Cd300afl/fl;ItgaxCre mice decreased to a level comparable to that seen in wild-type and Cd300afl/fl mice, respectively (Figure 2F and G).
evidence: Supported by experimental data in Figure 2F showing tumor growth after anti-CD25 treatment.

claim: After Treg cell depletion, the tumor volume of Cd300afl/fl;ItgaxCre mice decreased to a level comparable to that seen in Cd300afl/fl mice.
source: After Treg cell depletion, the tumor volume of the Cd300a−/− and Cd300afl/fl;ItgaxCre mice decreased to a level comparable to that seen in wild-type and Cd300afl/fl mice, respectively (Figure 2F and G).
evidence: Supported by experimental data in Figure 2G showing tumor growth after anti-CD25 treatment.

claim: Tumor-infiltrating CD8+ T cells in Cd300a−/− mice expressed significantly less IFN-γ than those in wild-type mice.
source: Tumor-infiltrating CD8+ T cells in Cd300a−/− mice expressed significantly less IFN-γ and significantly higher PD-1 than did those in wild-type mice (Figure 2H and I).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 2H.

claim: Tumor-infiltrating CD8+ T cells in Cd300a−/− mice expressed significantly higher PD-1 than those in wild-type mice.
source: Tumor-infiltrating CD8+ T cells in Cd300a−/− mice expressed significantly less IFN-γ and significantly higher PD-1 than did those in wild-type mice (Figure 2H and I).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 2I.

claim: The number of CD8+ T cells expressing both PD-1 and TIM-3 was significantly increased in Cd300afl/fl;ItgaxCre mice compared to Cd300afl/fl mice.
source: Moreover, the number of CD8+ T cells expressing both PD-1 and TIM-3 and those expressing CTLA-4 were significantly increased in Cd300afl/fl;ItgaxCre mice compared to Cd300afl/fl mice (Figure 2J and K), suggesting that tumor-infiltrating CD8+ T cells display more exhausted state in Cd300afl/fl;ItgaxCre mice than in Cd300afl/fl mice (Sawant et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 2J.

claim: The number of CD8+ T cells expressing CTLA-4 was significantly increased in Cd300afl/fl;ItgaxCre mice compared to Cd300afl/fl mice.
source: Moreover, the number of CD8+ T cells expressing both PD-1 and TIM-3 and those expressing CTLA-4 were significantly increased in Cd300afl/fl;ItgaxCre mice compared to Cd300afl/fl mice (Figure 2J and K), suggesting that tumor-infiltrating CD8+ T cells display more exhausted state in Cd300afl/fl;ItgaxCre mice than in Cd300afl/fl mice (Sawant et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 2K.

claim: Tumor-infiltrating CD8+ T cells display more exhausted state in Cd300afl/fl;ItgaxCre mice than in Cd300afl/fl mice.
source: Moreover, the number of CD8+ T cells expressing both PD-1 and TIM-3 and those expressing CTLA-4 were significantly increased in Cd300afl/fl;ItgaxCre mice compared to Cd300afl/fl mice (Figure 2J and K), suggesting that tumor-infiltrating CD8+ T cells display more exhausted state in Cd300afl/fl;ItgaxCre mice than in Cd300afl/fl mice (Sawant et al., 2019).
evidence: Inference based on increased expression of exhaustion markers and citation to published literature.

claim: CD300a on DCs regulates the number of tumor-infiltrating Treg cells, which suppress tumor immune responses.
source: These results suggest that CD300a on DCs regulates the number of tumor-infiltrating Treg cells, which suppress tumor immune responses.
evidence: Inference based on multiple experimental observations including Treg cell numbers, CD8+ T cell function, and tumor growth.

claim: A microbiota-mediated signal induces increased IFN-β production by DCs and increased numbers of Treg cells in the barrier tissues of Cd300a−/− mice relative to those of wild-type mice.
source: We previously reported that a microbiota-mediated signal induces increased IFN-β production by DCs and increased numbers of Treg cells in the barrier tissues such as the intestine, skin, and airway of Cd300a−/− mice relative to those of wild-type mice (Nakahashi-Oda et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous publication by the authors.

claim: The expression of Ifnb was higher in DCs in the tumor tissues of Cd300a−/− mice than in those of wild-type mice.
source: In the current study, we found that the expression of Ifnb was also higher in DCs in the tumor tissues of Cd300a−/− and Cd300afl/fl;ItgaxCre mice than in those of wild-type and Cd300afl/fl mice, resepectively (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: Supported by quantitative RT-PCR data in Figure 3A.

claim: The expression of Ifnb was higher in DCs in the tumor tissues of Cd300afl/fl;ItgaxCre mice than in those of Cd300afl/fl mice.
source: In the current study, we found that the expression of Ifnb was also higher in DCs in the tumor tissues of Cd300a−/− and Cd300afl/fl;ItgaxCre mice than in those of wild-type and Cd300afl/fl mice, resepectively (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: Supported by quantitative RT-PCR data in Figure 3B.

claim: Cd300a−/− mice raised under germ-free conditions showed larger numbers of Treg cells than wild-type mice raised under germ-free conditions.
source: In contrast to the barrier tissues, Cd300a−/− mice still showed larger numbers of Treg cells and a larger tumor volume than did wild-type mice raised under GF conditions (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by immunohistochemistry data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Cd300a−/− mice raised under germ-free conditions showed larger tumor volume than wild-type mice raised under germ-free conditions.
source: In contrast to the barrier tissues, Cd300a−/− mice still showed larger numbers of Treg cells and a larger tumor volume than did wild-type mice raised under GF conditions (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by tumor growth data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The microbiota-mediated signal was dispensable for the increased numbers of Treg cells in the tumor of Cd300a−/− mice.
source: These results suggest that, unlike in the barrier tissues, the microbiota-mediated signal was dispensable for the increased numbers of Treg cells in the tumor and for the enhanced tumor growth in Cd300a−/− mice.
evidence: Inference based on comparable phenotype in germ-free conditions.

claim: The microbiota-mediated signal was dispensable for the enhanced tumor growth in Cd300a−/− mice.
source: These results suggest that, unlike in the barrier tissues, the microbiota-mediated signal was dispensable for the increased numbers of Treg cells in the tumor and for the enhanced tumor growth in Cd300a−/− mice.
evidence: Inference based on comparable phenotype in germ-free conditions.

claim: Solid tumors lapse into necrosis in the core region under conditions of hypoxia and low pH, resulting in the secretion of several immune stimulators.
source: Solid tumors lapse into necrosis in the core region under conditions of hypoxia and low pH, resulting in the secretion of several immune stimulators, such as damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs), DNA, RNA (Patidar et al., 2018), and EVs (Couto et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Four hours after incubation in the presence of B16 melanoma culture supernatant, Cd300a−/− BMDCs expressed higher levels of Ifnb than wild-type BMDCs.
source: Four hours after incubation in the presence of the culture supernatant, Cd300a−/− BMDCs expressed higher levels of Ifnb than did wild-type BMDCs (Figure 3C), suggesting that CD300a suppressed the Ifnb expression induced by a tumor-derived immune mediator in the culture supernatant.
evidence: Supported by quantitative RT-PCR data in Figure 3C.

claim: CD300a suppressed the Ifnb expression induced by a tumor-derived immune mediator in the culture supernatant.
source: Four hours after incubation in the presence of the culture supernatant, Cd300a−/− BMDCs expressed higher levels of Ifnb than did wild-type BMDCs (Figure 3C), suggesting that CD300a suppressed the Ifnb expression induced by a tumor-derived immune mediator in the culture supernatant.
evidence: Inference based on differential Ifnb expression between wild-type and Cd300a−/− BMDCs.

claim: EVs are particles released from cells that are delimited by a lipid bilayer that contains phosphatidylserine.
source: Since EVs are the particles released from the cells that are delimited by a lipid bilayer that contains phosphatidylserine (Lima et al., 2009), the ligand for CD300a (Nakahashi-Oda et al., 2012a), and containing functional biomolecules (van Niel et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Phosphatidylserine is the ligand for CD300a.
source: Since EVs are the particles released from the cells that are delimited by a lipid bilayer that contains phosphatidylserine (Lima et al., 2009), the ligand for CD300a (Nakahashi-Oda et al., 2012a), and containing functional biomolecules (van Niel et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous publication by the authors.

claim: Purified TEVs expressed phosphatidylserine on the surface.
source: We purified TEVs from the culture supernatants of B16 melanoma cells by centrifugation and phosphatidylserine receptor-conjugated beads (Figure 3D and E), which indeed expressed phosphatidylserine on the surface and bound to a chimeric fusion protein of the extracellular portion of CD300a with human IgG1 (Figure 3F).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 3F showing PS staining.

claim: Purified TEVs bound to a chimeric fusion protein of the extracellular portion of CD300a with human IgG1.
source: We purified TEVs from the culture supernatants of B16 melanoma cells by centrifugation and phosphatidylserine receptor-conjugated beads (Figure 3D and E), which indeed expressed phosphatidylserine on the surface and bound to a chimeric fusion protein of the extracellular portion of CD300a with human IgG1 (Figure 3F).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 3F showing CD300a Fc binding.

claim: Stimulation with purified TEVs induced higher Ifnb expression in Cd300a−/− BMDCs than in wild-type BMDCs.
source: Stimulation with the purified TEVs induced higher Ifnb expression in Cd300a−/− BMDCs than in wild-type BMDCs (Figure 3G).
evidence: Supported by quantitative RT-PCR data in Figure 3G.

claim: Cd300a−/− BMDCs showed decreased Ifnb expression to a level comparable to wild-type BMDC when cultured in B16 melanoma culture supernatants after removal of TEVs.
source: However, Cd300a−/− BMDCs showed decreased Ifnb expression to a level comparable to wild-type BMDC when these BMMCs were cultured in the culture supernatants of B16 melanoma cells after removal of TEVs by phosphatidylserine receptor-conjugated beads (Figure 3H).
evidence: Supported by quantitative RT-PCR data in Figure 3H.

claim: Neither wild-type nor Cd300a−/− BMDCs expressed IFN-β after stimulation with HMGB-1.
source: In contrast, neither wild-type nor Cd300a−/− BMDCs expressed IFN-β after stimulation high-mobility group box-1 protein (HMGB-1) (Figure 3G) a well-known DAMP, which can be released by damaged tumors.
evidence: Supported by quantitative RT-PCR data in Figure 3G.

claim: The interaction of CD300a with PS on TEVs suppressed Ifnb expression in BMDCs.
source: These results suggest that the interaction of CD300a with PS on TEVs suppressed Ifnb expression in BMDCs.
evidence: Inference based on differential Ifnb expression and PS masking experiments.

claim: Ifnb expression in Cd300a−/− BMDCs was decreased to a level comparable to that seen in wild-type BMDCs after stimulation with TEVs whose PS was masked with D89E-MFG-E8.
source: Indeed, Ifnb expression in Cd300a−/− BMDCs was decreased to a level comparable to that seen in wild-type BMDCs after stimulation with TEVs whose PS was masked with MFG-E8 protein mutated at residue 89 (D89E-MFG-E8) (Nakahashi-Oda et al., 2012a; Figure 3I).
evidence: Supported by quantitative RT-PCR data in Figure 3I.

claim: TEVs suppressed Ifnb expression in BMDCs via interaction between CD300a on BMDCs and PS on TEVs.
source: Together, these results indicated that TEVs suppressed Ifnb expression in BMDCs via interaction between CD300a on BMDCs and PS on TEVs.
evidence: Inference based on multiple experimental observations including PS masking and EV depletion.

claim: TEV-stimulated Cd300a−/− BMDCs increased the number of Treg cells to a greater extent than TEV-stimulated wild-type BMDCs when cocultured with naive CD4+ T cells.
source: TEV-stimulated Cd300a−/− BMDCs increased the number of Treg cells to a greater extent than did TEV-stimulated wild-type BMDCs (Figure 4A).
evidence: Supported by coculture experiment data in Figure 4A.

claim: Addition of a neutralizing anti-IFN-β antibody to the coculture of Treg cells and Cd300a−/− BMDCs reduced the Treg cell numbers to a level comparable to that seen in the coculture of Treg cells and wild-type BMDCs.
source: Addition of a neutralizing anti-IFN-β antibody to the coculture of Treg cells and Cd300a−/− BMDCs reduced the Treg cell numbers to a level comparable to that seen in the coculture of Treg cells and wild-type BMDCs (Figure 4A).
evidence: Supported by coculture experiment data in Figure 4A with anti-IFN-β treatment.

claim: Administration of a neutralizing anti-IFN-β antibody reduced tumor volume in Cd300afl/fl;ItgaxCre mice to a comparable level of that in Cd300afl/fl mice.
source: Moreover, administration of a neutralizing anti-IFN-β antibody showed reduced tumor volume in Cd300afl/fl;ItgaxCre mice to a comparable level of that in Cd300afl/fl mice (Figure 4B), suggesting that IFN-β augmented Treg cell proliferation or survival and promoted tumor progression in Cd300afl/fl;ItgaxCre mice.
evidence: Supported by tumor growth data in Figure 4B.

claim: IFN-β augmented Treg cell proliferation or survival and promoted tumor progression in Cd300afl/fl;ItgaxCre mice.
source: Moreover, administration of a neutralizing anti-IFN-β antibody showed reduced tumor volume in Cd300afl/fl;ItgaxCre mice to a comparable level of that in Cd300afl/fl mice (Figure 4B), suggesting that IFN-β augmented Treg cell proliferation or survival and promoted tumor progression in Cd300afl/fl;ItgaxCre mice.
evidence: Inference based on anti-IFN-β antibody treatment reducing tumor growth.

claim: Treatment with GW4869 led to a significant decrease in the number of tumor-infiltrating Treg cells in Cd300a−/− mice to a comparable level of those in wild-type mice.
source: Treatment with GW4869, which inhibits EV release from tumors and DCs, led to a significant decrease in the number of tumor-infiltrating Treg cells and the tumor volume in Cd300a−/− and Cd300afl/fl;ItgaxCre mice to a comparable level of those in wild-type and Cd300afl/fl mice, respectively (Figure 4C-E).
evidence: Supported by immunohistochemistry data in Figure 4C.

claim: Treatment with GW4869 led to a significant decrease in tumor volume in Cd300a−/− mice to a comparable level of those in wild-type mice.
source: Treatment with GW4869, which inhibits EV release from tumors and DCs, led to a significant decrease in the number of tumor-infiltrating Treg cells and the tumor volume in Cd300a−/− and Cd300afl/fl;ItgaxCre mice to a comparable level of those in wild-type and Cd300afl/fl mice, respectively (Figure 4C-E).
evidence: Supported by tumor growth data in Figure 4D.

claim: Treatment with GW4869 led to a significant decrease in the number of tumor-infiltrating Treg cells in Cd300afl/fl;ItgaxCre mice to a comparable level of those in Cd300afl/fl mice.
source: Treatment with GW4869, which inhibits EV release from tumors and DCs, led to a significant decrease in the number of tumor-infiltrating Treg cells and the tumor volume in Cd300a−/− and Cd300afl/fl;ItgaxCre mice to a comparable level of those in wild-type and Cd300afl/fl mice, respectively (Figure 4C-E).
evidence: Supported by immunohistochemistry data in Figure 4C.

claim: Treatment with GW4869 led to a significant decrease in tumor volume in Cd300afl/fl;ItgaxCre mice to a comparable level of those in Cd300afl/fl mice.
source: Treatment with GW4869, which inhibits EV release from tumors and DCs, led to a significant decrease in the number of tumor-infiltrating Treg cells and the tumor volume in Cd300a−/− and Cd300afl/fl;ItgaxCre mice to a comparable level of those in wild-type and Cd300afl/fl mice, respectively (Figure 4C-E).
evidence: Supported by tumor growth data in Figure 4E.

claim: CD300a suppresses TEV-mediated IFN-β production, resulting in a decrease in the Treg cell population and the suppression of tumor development.
source: These results nevertheless indicate that CD300a suppresses TEV-mediated IFN-β production, resulting in a decrease in the Treg cell population and the suppression of tumor development.
evidence: Inference based on multiple experimental observations including EV inhibition, IFN-β neutralization, and Treg cell depletion.

claim: TEVs were incorporated into endosomes in both wild-type and Cd300a−/− DCs.
source: We found that the TEVs were incorporated into endosomes, as identified by the expression of endosome antigen (EEA)-1, in both genotypes of DCs (Figure 5A).
evidence: Supported by confocal microscopy data in Figure 5A showing colocalization with EEA-1.

claim: The number of TEVs in the endosomes was comparable between wild-type and Cd300a−/− BMDCs.
source: The number of TEVs in the endosomes was comparable between wild-type and Cd300a−/− BMDCs (Figure 5B), suggesting that CD300a did not affect TEV incorporation into the endosomes.
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 5B measuring PKH-labeled EV uptake.

claim: CD300a did not affect TEV incorporation into the endosomes.
source: The number of TEVs in the endosomes was comparable between wild-type and Cd300a−/− BMDCs (Figure 5B), suggesting that CD300a did not affect TEV incorporation into the endosomes.
evidence: Inference based on comparable EV uptake between genotypes.

claim: CD300a was internalized from the cell surface into the endosomes after coculture of BMDCs with TEVs.
source: Interestingly, we also found that CD300a was internalized from the cell surface into the endosomes, an event that might be mediated by the tyrosine-based sorting motif in the cytoplasmic region of CD300a (Yotsumoto et al., 2003), after coculture of BMDCs with TEVs (Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by confocal microscopy data in Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: TEVs colocalized with CD300a at the endosomes.
source: As a result, the TEVs colocalized with CD300a at the endosomes (Figure 5A and C).
evidence: Supported by confocal microscopy data in Figure 5A and C.

claim: CD300a was activated via stimulation with TEVs at the endosomes.
source: Given that EVs expose phosphatidylserine on their lipid bilayer, which is a CD300a ligand, these results suggest that CD300a was activated via stimulation with TEVs at the endosomes.
evidence: Inference based on colocalization of CD300a with TEVs at endosomes and PS on TEVs.

claim: TLR3 inhibitor decreased Ifnb expression in Cd300a−/− BMDCs to a level comparable to that in wild-type BMDCs after coculture with TEVs.
source: To examine whether CD300a inhibited TLR3-mediated signaling at the endosomes upon stimulation with TEVs, we cocultured wild-type and Cd300a−/− BMDCs with TEVs in the presence of an inhibitor of TLR3 (Cheng et al., 2011). This inhibitor decreased Ifnb expression in Cd300a−/− BMDCs to a level comparable to that in wild-type BMDCs (Figure 5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Supported by quantitative RT-PCR data in Figure 5D.

claim: TLR4 inhibitor did not affect the expression of Ifnb in either wild-type or Cd300a−/− BMDCs after coculture with TEVs.
source: In contrast, the TLR4 inhibitor TKA-242 did not affect the expression of Ifnb in either BMDC genotype (Figure 5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Supported by quantitative RT-PCR data in Figure 5D.

claim: CD300a inhibits TLR3-mediated signaling for IFN-β production.
source: These results suggest that CD300a inhibits TLR3-mediated signaling for IFN-β production.
evidence: Inference based on TLR3 inhibitor experiments.

claim: The expression of Ifnb in ticam-1−/−;Cd300a−/− BMDCs was decreased to the comparable level of that in ticam-1−/− BMDCs after coculture with TEVs.
source: Moreover, the expression of Ifnb in ticam-1−/−;Cd300a−/− BMDCs was also decreased to the comparable level of that in ticam-1−/− BMDCs after coculture with TEVs (Figure 5E).
evidence: Supported by quantitative RT-PCR data in Figure 5E.

claim: The phosphorylation level of IRF3 was increased to a greater extent in EV-stimulated Cd300a−/− BMDCs than in wild-type BMDCs.
source: In addition, we found that the phosphorylation level of interferon regulatory factor 3 (IRF3), a downstream molecule of the TRIF signaling pathway, was increased to a greater extent in EV-stimulated Cd300a−/− BMDCs than in wild-type BMDCs (Figure 5F).
evidence: Supported by Western blot data in Figure 5F.

claim: Tumor growth was significantly larger for B16 melanoma-injected Myd88−/−;Cd300a−/− mice compared with B16-injected Myd88−/− mice.
source: In vivo analyses also showed that, although tumor growth was significantly larger and the survival rate was significantly shorter for B16 melanoma-injected Myd88−/−;Cd300a−/− mice compared with B16-injected Myd88−/− mice, tumor development and survival did not differ between ticam-1−/−;Cd300a−/− and ticam-1−/− mice (Figure 5G-J).
evidence: Supported by tumor growth data in Figure 5I.

claim: The survival rate was significantly shorter for B16 melanoma-injected Myd88−/−;Cd300a−/− mice compared with B16-injected Myd88−/− mice.
source: In vivo analyses also showed that, although tumor growth was significantly larger and the survival rate was significantly shorter for B16 melanoma-injected Myd88−/−;Cd300a−/− mice compared with B16-injected Myd88−/− mice, tumor development and survival did not differ between ticam-1−/−;Cd300a−/− and ticam-1−/− mice (Figure 5G-J).
evidence: Supported by survival data in Figure 5J.

claim: Tumor development did not differ between ticam-1−/−;Cd300a−/− and ticam-1−/− mice.
source: In vivo analyses also showed that, although tumor growth was significantly larger and the survival rate was significantly shorter for B16 melanoma-injected Myd88−/−;Cd300a−/− mice compared with B16-injected Myd88−/− mice, tumor development and survival did not differ between ticam-1−/−;Cd300a−/− and ticam-1−/− mice (Figure 5G-J).
evidence: Supported by tumor growth data in Figure 5G.

claim: Survival did not differ between ticam-1−/−;Cd300a−/− and ticam-1−/− mice after B16 melanoma injection.
source: In vivo analyses also showed that, although tumor growth was significantly larger and the survival rate was significantly shorter for B16 melanoma-injected Myd88−/−;Cd300a−/− mice compared with B16-injected Myd88−/− mice, tumor development and survival did not differ between ticam-1−/−;Cd300a−/− and ticam-1−/− mice (Figure 5G-J).
evidence: Supported by survival data in Figure 5H.

claim: CD300a inhibits the TLR3–TRIF signaling pathway for IFN-β production at the endosomes in DCs, resulting in the suppression of Treg cell activation and tumor development.
source: Taken together, these data suggest that CD300a inhibits the TLR3–TRIF signaling pathway for IFN-β production at the endosomes in DCs, resulting in the suppression of Treg cell activation and tumor development.
evidence: Inference based on multiple experimental observations including TLR3 inhibition, TRIF pathway analysis, and in vivo tumor studies.

claim: CD300A is expressed on populations that express HLA-DR, ITGAX (CD11C), ITGAM (CD11B), CD14, and CD163 in human melanoma tissues.
source: To examine the role of CD300A in tumor development in humans, we analyzed the data on the single-cell RNA sequence (scRNA-seq) of human melanoma tissues, which demonstrated that CD300A is expressed on populations that express HLA-DR, ITGAX (CD11C), ITGAM (CD11B), CD14, and CD163 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1), consistent with the results of mouse melanoma.
evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq data analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: SKCM patients expressing low levels of CD300A mRNA had shorter survival times than those expressing higher CD300A mRNA levels.
source: We further analyzed the database of the Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) project and found that skin cutaneous melanoma (SKCM) patients expressing low levels of CD300A mRNA had shorter survival times than did those expressing higher CD300A mRNA levels (Figure 6A).
evidence: Supported by TCGA database analysis shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The expression ratio of CD300A to ITGAX is negatively correlated with that of FOXP3 to CD8A in melanoma patients.
source: We also found that the expression ratio of CD300A to ITGAX is negatively correlated with that of FOXP3 to CD8A (Figure 6B).
evidence: Supported by correlation analysis of TCGA data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: CD300A suppressed Treg cell proliferation and/or activation and tumor development in humans.
source: These results suggested that CD300A suppressed Treg cell proliferation and/or activation and tumor development.
evidence: Inference based on correlation between CD300A expression and FOXP3/CD8A ratio in human melanoma.

claim: Patients with melanoma showed strong positive correlation between FOXP3 and IFNB1 expression.
source: Moreover, we found that patients with melanoma showed strong positive correlation between FOXP3 and IFNB1 expression (Figure 6C).
evidence: Supported by correlation analysis of TCGA data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: TCGA database of SKCM showed a strong positive correlation between expressions of SMPD3 and IFNB1 in melanoma tissues.
source: Neutral sphingomyelinase-2 (SMPD3), which is a target of an inhibitor of EV-release GW4869, enhances TEV release from tumor cells (Kosaka et al., 2013; Kosaka et al., 2010). TCGA database of SKCM also showed a strong positive correlation between expressions of SMPD3 and IFNB1 in melanoma tissues (Figure 6D), suggesting that TEVs increased IFN-β expression in human melanoma tissues.
evidence: Supported by correlation analysis of TCGA data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: TEVs increased IFN-β expression in human melanoma tissues.
source: TCGA database of SKCM also showed a strong positive correlation between expressions of SMPD3 and IFNB1 in melanoma tissues (Figure 6D), suggesting that TEVs increased IFN-β expression in human melanoma tissues.
evidence: Inference based on correlation between SMPD3 (EV release enzyme) and IFNB1 expression.

claim: CD300A might augment tumor immunity via suppression of tumor-infiltrating Treg cells in humans.
source: These results were consistent with those of mouse models of melanoma development in the current study. Taken together, these results suggested that CD300A might augment tumor immunity via suppression of tumor-infiltrating Treg cells also in humans.
evidence: Inference based on human data being consistent with mouse model findings.

claim: TEV-stimulated DCs produce IFN-β via TLR3 at the endosomes, resulting in increased number of tumor-infiltrating Treg cells and exacerbation of tumor development.
source: Although the biological roles of EVs have been reported from various angles, how EVs regulate immune responses is not yet fully understood. In the present study, we showed that TEV-stimulated DCs for IFN-β production via TLR3 at the endosomes, resulting in the increased number of tumor-infiltrating Treg cells and thus the exacerbation of tumor development.
evidence: Summary inference based on multiple experimental findings throughout the study.

claim: TEVs stimulated CD300a and inhibited TEV-mediated TLR3 signaling at the endosome.
source: In contrast, the TEVs also stimulated CD300a and inhibited TEV-mediated TLR3 signaling at the endosome.
evidence: Summary inference based on experimental findings showing CD300a internalization and TLR3 inhibition.

claim: TEVs have both positive and negative functions in the regulation of IFN-β production and Treg activation via the axis of EV-derived RNA-TLR3 and EV-derived phosphatidylserine-CD300a.
source: Thus, TEVs have both positive and negative functions in the regulation of IFN-β production and Treg activation via the axis of EV-derived RNA-TLR3 and EV-derived phosphatidylserine-CD300a, respectively.
evidence: Summary inference based on the dual role of TEVs in activating TLR3 and CD300a.

claim: The Treg cells in tumor microenvironments is regulated by the balance of positive and negative signaling for IFN-β production induced by TEV.
source: These results suggest that the Treg cells in tumor microenvironments is regulated by the balance of positive and negative signaling for IFN-β production induced by TEV (Figure 7).
evidence: Summary inference based on the opposing effects of TLR3 and CD300a signaling.

claim: Higher expression of CD300A was associated with lower expression of Foxp3 in melanoma patients.
source: Indeed, we showed that higher expression of CD300A was associated with lower expression of Foxp3 and longer survival times of melanoma patients.
evidence: Supported by TCGA database analysis showing negative correlation.

claim: Higher expression of CD300A was associated with longer survival times of melanoma patients.
source: Indeed, we showed that higher expression of CD300A was associated with lower expression of Foxp3 and longer survival times of melanoma patients.
evidence: Supported by TCGA database survival analysis.

claim: Human melanoma tissues showed quite low CD300A expression in T cells compared to high expression in the myeloid cells.
source: Though human CD300A is reported to be expressed on the subsets of T cells in peripheral blood (Borrego, 2013), human melanoma tissues showed quite low CD300A expression in T cells compared to high expression in the myeloid cells.
evidence: Inference based on scRNA-seq analysis of human melanoma tissues.

claim: TEVs promoted Treg cell expansion through DC-independent manner in vitro.
source: While previous reports demonstrated that TEVs promoted Treg cell expansion through DC-independent manner in vitro (Muller et al., 2017; Szajnik et al., 2010; Wieckowski et al., 2009), the current study first demonstrated that TEVs regulate Treg cell activation and tumor development in vivo by DCs in the tumor microenvironment.
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature.

claim: TEVs regulate Treg cell activation and tumor development in vivo by DCs in the tumor microenvironment.
source: While previous reports demonstrated that TEVs promoted Treg cell expansion through DC-independent manner in vitro (Muller et al., 2017; Szajnik et al., 2010; Wieckowski et al., 2009), the current study first demonstrated that TEVs regulate Treg cell activation and tumor development in vivo by DCs in the tumor microenvironment.
evidence: Summary of the study's novel findings based on in vivo experiments.

claim: The conventional type-1 DC (cDC1) expresses the chemokine receptor XCR1 and CD103 and lower amount of CD11b and has the high ability to migrate from tumors to lymph nodes and presents a tumor antigen to CD8+ T cells.
source: The conventional type-1 DC (cDC1) expresses the chemokine receptor XCR1 and CD103 and lower amount of CD11b that has the high ability to migrate from tumors to lymph nodes and presents a tumor antigen to CD8+ T cells (Bedoui et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature.

claim: The conventional type-2 DC (cDC2) are commonly distinguished from cDC1 by their preferential expression of higher amount of CD11b.
source: In contrast, the conventional type-2 DC (cDC2) are commonly distinguished from cDC1 by their preferential expression of higher amount of CD11b.
evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge about DC subsets.

claim: cDC2 are predominantly involved in antigen presentation by MHC class II to CD4+ T cells.
source: cDC2 are predominantly involved in antigen presentation by MHC class II to CD4+ T cells (Gao et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature.

claim: CD300a on cDC2, rather than cDC1, may regulate Treg cells activation by inhibiting the TLR3–IFN-β pathway in tumor microenvironment.
source: Given that cDC2 is involved in CD4+ T cell differentiation and activation, CD300a on cDC2, rather than cDC1, may regulate Treg cells activation by inhibiting the TLR3–IFN-β pathway in tumor microenvironment.
evidence: Speculation based on known functions of cDC2 and the study's findings.

claim: Type I IFNs are key players in antiviral and anticancer immune response by upregulating both cross-presentation of antigens by CD8a+ DCs and cytotoxic activity of CD8+ T cells and NK cells.
source: Type I IFNs are key players in antiviral and anticancer immune response by upregulating both cross-presentation of antigens by CD8a+ DCs and cytotoxic activity of CD8+ T cells and NK cells (Zitvogel et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature.

claim: The current clinical use of IFN-β for cancers showed limited efficiency.
source: However, the current clinical use of IFN-β for cancers showed limited efficiency (Medrano et al., 2017; Minn, 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Type I IFNs have immunosuppressive functions, such as inducing the production of IL-10.
source: This may be partly due to the fact that type I IFNs also have immunosuppressive functions, such as inducing the production of IL-10, an immunosuppressive cytokine (Snell et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature.

claim: On Treg cells, IFNs are most potent cytokines to induce PD-L1.
source: In addition, on Treg cells, IFNs are most potent cytokines to induce PD-L1 (Morimoto et al., 2018; Xiao et al., 2018), which contributes to sustain Foxp3 expression and promotes the function of Treg cells (Francisco et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature.

claim: PD-L1 contributes to sustain Foxp3 expression and promotes the function of Treg cells.
source: In addition, on Treg cells, IFNs are most potent cytokines to induce PD-L1 (Morimoto et al., 2018; Xiao et al., 2018), which contributes to sustain Foxp3 expression and promotes the function of Treg cells (Francisco et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature.

claim: IFN-α/β receptor signaling promotes Treg cell development.
source: In addition, IFN-α/β receptor signaling promotes Treg cell development (Metidji et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature.

claim: Gut commensals stimulated CX3CR1+CD103− CD11b+ DCs to produce IFN-β, which augmented the proliferation of Treg cells in the intestine.
source: We previously reported that gut commensals stimulated CX3CR1+CD103− CD11b+ DCs to produce IFN-β, which augmented the proliferation of Treg cells in the intestine (Nakahashi-Oda et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous publication by the authors.

claim: In viral infection and tumor microenvironment, type I IFNs directly inhibit the proliferation and activation of Treg cells.
source: In contrast, published reports demonstrated that, in viral infection and tumor microenvironment, type I IFNs directly inhibit the proliferation and activation of Treg cells (Gangaplara et al., 2018; Srivastava et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature.

claim: CD300a inhibited the CD14-mediated TLR4 internalization in CD11b+ DCs induced by gut microbiota.
source: We have previously reported that CD300a inhibited the CD14-mediated TLR4 internalization in CD11b+ DCs induced by gut microbiota (Nakahashi-Oda et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous publication by the authors.

claim: Internalization of TLR4 by CD14 induces activation of the TRIF pathway to produce IFN-β, but not MyD88 pathway.
source: This internalization of TLR4 by CD14 induces activation of the TRIF pathway to produce IFN-β, but not MyD88 pathway.
evidence: Based on established knowledge of TLR4 signaling pathways.

claim: CD300a specifically inhibits TRIF signaling to produce IFN-β, rather than the MyD88-mediated signaling pathway stimulated by LPS and HMGB-1.
source: In the present study, we also found that CD300a inhibits TLR3-mediated TRIF signaling to produce IFN-β (Figure 5D and E). These data suggest that CD300a specifically inhibits TRIF signaling to produce IFN-β, rather than the MyD88-mediated signaling pathway stimulated by LPS and HMGB-1.
evidence: Inference based on experimental data showing CD300a inhibits TRIF but not MyD88 pathways.

claim: TLR3 activates PI3 kinase and the downstream kinase, Akt, leading to full phosphorylation and activation of IRF3.
source: TLR3 activates PI3 kinase and the downstream kinase, Akt, leading to full phosphorylation and activation of IRF3 (Sarkar et al., 2004).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature.

claim: IRF3 phosphorylation was increased in Cd300a−/− DCs compared with wild-type DCs after stimulation with TEV.
source: Indeed, we showed that IRF3 phosphorylation was increased in Cd300a−/− DCs compared with wild-type DCs after stimulation with TEV.
evidence: Supported by Western blot data in Figure 5F.

claim: TLR3 on alveolar epithelial cells recognized RNAs in TEV and promoted lung metastasis.
source: Recent studies have revealed that TLR3 on alveolar epithelial cells recognized RNAs in TEV and promoted lung metastasis (Liu et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature.

claim: The role of RNAs in TEV is dependent on target cells.
source: Therefore, the role of RNAs in TEV is dependent on target cells.
evidence: Inference based on different outcomes of TEV-RNA recognition in different cell types.

claim: More than 4000 trillion EVs are presumed to be in the blood of cancer patients.
source: More than 4000 trillion EVs are presumed to be in the blood of cancer patients (Melo et al., 2015) and EVs released from tumor cells (tumor-derived EVs [TEVs]) are emerging as critical messengers in tumor progression and metastasis (Couto et al., 2018; Grange et al., 2011; Melo et al., 2015; Skog et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature.

claim: EVs released from tumor cells are emerging as critical messengers in tumor progression and metastasis.
source: More than 4000 trillion EVs are presumed to be in the blood of cancer patients (Melo et al., 2015) and EVs released from tumor cells (tumor-derived EVs [TEVs]) are emerging as critical messengers in tumor progression and metastasis (Couto et al., 2018; Grange et al., 2011; Melo et al., 2015; Skog et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Fas ligand and PD-L1 on the surface of TEV induce apoptosis or suppression of activated T cells.
source: In tumor immunity, pleiotropic and deleterious role of TEV has been reported that, Fas ligand and PD-L1, the immunomodulatory molecules, on the surface of TEV induce apoptosis or suppression of activated T cells (Andreola et al., 2002; Chen et al., 2018) and TGF-β1 in TEV induces Treg cells (Clayton et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature.

claim: TGF-β1 in TEV induces Treg cells.
source: In tumor immunity, pleiotropic and deleterious role of TEV has been reported that, Fas ligand and PD-L1, the immunomodulatory molecules, on the surface of TEV induce apoptosis or suppression of activated T cells (Andreola et al., 2002; Chen et al., 2018) and TGF-β1 in TEV induces Treg cells (Clayton et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature.

claim: TEV upregulates PD-L1 expression on myeloid cells.
source: TEV also upregulates PD-L1 expression on myeloid cells (Fleming et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature.

claim: Myeloid cells that capture microRNA within TEVs are altered to myeloid-derived suppressor cells and/or M2 macrophages and promote the malignant behavior of cancers.
source: Furthermore, myeloid cells that capture microRNA within TEVs are altered to myeloid-derived suppressor cells and/or M2 macrophages and promote the malignant behavior of cancers (Huber et al., 2018; Tian et al., 2019; Wang et al., 2018; Ying et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature.

claim: TEVs play a key role in the suppression of antitumor immune responses.
source: These intensive investigations have shown that TEVs play a key role in the suppression of antitumor immune responses (Zebrowska et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature.

claim: Tumor-infiltrating regulatory T cells play a pivotal role in tumor immunity.
source: Although tumor-infiltrating regulatory T (Treg) cells play a pivotal role in tumor immunity, how Treg cell activation are regulated in tumor microenvironments remains unclear.
evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge about Treg cells in tumors.

claim: Mice deficient in CD300a on their dendritic cells have increased numbers of Treg cells in tumors after transplantation of B16 melanoma.
source: Here, we found that mice deficient in the inhibitory immunoreceptor CD300a on their dendritic cells (DCs) have increased numbers of Treg cells in tumors and greater tumor growth compared with wild-type mice after transplantation of B16 melanoma.
evidence: Summary of key findings from the study.

claim: Mice deficient in CD300a on their dendritic cells have greater tumor growth compared with wild-type mice after transplantation of B16 melanoma.
source: Here, we found that mice deficient in the inhibitory immunoreceptor CD300a on their dendritic cells (DCs) have increased numbers of Treg cells in tumors and greater tumor growth compared with wild-type mice after transplantation of B16 melanoma.
evidence: Summary of key findings from the study.

claim: Pharmacological impairment of extracellular vesicle release decreased Treg cell numbers in CD300a-deficient mice.
source: Pharmacological impairment of extracellular vesicle (EV) release decreased Treg cell numbers in CD300a-deficient mice.
evidence: Summary of key findings from the study using GW4869.

claim: Coculture of DCs with tumor-derived EV induced the internalization of CD300a and the incorporation of EVs into endosomes.
source: Coculture of DCs with tumor-derived EV (TEV) induced the internalization of CD300a and the incorporation of EVs into endosomes, in which CD300a inhibited TEV-mediated TLR3–TRIF signaling for activation of the IFN-β-Treg cells axis.
evidence: Summary of key mechanistic findings from the study.

claim: CD300a inhibited TEV-mediated TLR3–TRIF signaling for activation of the IFN-β-Treg cells axis in endosomes.
source: Coculture of DCs with tumor-derived EV (TEV) induced the internalization of CD300a and the incorporation of EVs into endosomes, in which CD300a inhibited TEV-mediated TLR3–TRIF signaling for activation of the IFN-β-Treg cells axis.
evidence: Summary of key mechanistic findings from the study.

claim: Higher expression of CD300A was associated with decreased tumor-infiltrating Treg cells in patients with melanoma.
source: We also show that higher expression of CD300A was associated with decreased tumor-infiltrating Treg cells and longer survival time in patients with melanoma.
evidence: Summary of key findings from human data analysis.

claim: Higher expression of CD300A was associated with longer survival time in patients with melanoma.
source: We also show that higher expression of CD300A was associated with decreased tumor-infiltrating Treg cells and longer survival time in patients with melanoma.
evidence: Summary of key findings from human data analysis.
